subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literary Analysis: University-Level Essay Writing
subjects.summary: Students develop the analytical writing skills required for first-year university — constructing complex arguments, integrating sources, and writing with precision and intellectual authority.

quiz.q: A university-level literary argument differs from a high school argument in that ___.

options: university requires less reading

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Polynomial Functions: Deep Dive into Graphs and Equations
subjects.summary: Students investigate polynomial functions of all degrees — connecting multiplicity of zeros, end behaviour, turning points, and algebraic form to graphical behaviour.

quiz.q: A polynomial of degree n can have at most ___ real zeros and at most ___ turning points.

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Introduction to Limits and Continuity
subjects.summary: Students develop an intuitive and rigorous understanding of limits — what they mean, how to evaluate them, and their role as the foundation of calculus.

the derivative exists at a

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Kinematics in 2D: Projectile Motion
subjects.summary: Students analyse projectile motion by decomposing it into independent horizontal and vertical components, applying kinematic equations to each.

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Independent Study: The Novel — Form and Meaning

options: a plot summary with quotations
only a character description

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Rational Functions: Analysis and Graphing
subjects.summary: Students perform complete analysis of rational functions — identifying all asymptotes, holes, intercepts, and behaviour — and graph them without technology.

subjects.title: Literary Device: The Pathetic Fallacy in Nature Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: the pathetic fallacy is a literary device, coined by critic John Ruskin, in which human emotions are attributed to non-human elements of nature, allowing a landscape or the weather to mirror a character's inner state.

quiz.q: The pathetic fallacy attributes ___ to non-human elements of nature.
options: Scientific data
Human emotions
A precise chronology
Grammatical rules

quiz.q: The term "pathetic fallacy" was coined by the critic ___.
options: William Shakespeare
Virginia Woolf
John Ruskin
Henry David Thoreau

quiz.q: Which is an example of the pathetic fallacy in a story?
options: A character explains a scientific fact about rainfall
A stormy sky mirrors a character's inner turmoil
A narrator lists the exact date of an event
A character describes the layout of a room

quiz.q: Why might a writer use the pathetic fallacy rather than directly stating a character's emotions?
options: It has no effect on how a scene is experienced by the reader
It can create mood and atmosphere indirectly, letting setting reflect feeling
Direct statements of emotion are always considered better writing
This device removes all emotional content from a scene

quiz.q: How does the pathetic fallacy differ from ordinary personification?
options: They are identical with no meaningful difference
The pathetic fallacy specifically involves nature or weather reflecting human emotion, while personification is broader
Personification only applies to inanimate objects, never nature
The pathetic fallacy never involves any element of nature

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Laws of Logarithms: Product, Quotient, and Power Rules
subjects.summary: Students learn and apply the product, quotient, and power laws of logarithms to expand and condense logarithmic expressions.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Laws of Logarithms: Product, Quotient, and Power Rules

quiz.q: Which expression is equivalent to log_b(xy)?
options: log_b x · log_b y
log_b(x)/log_b(y)
log_b x - log_b y
log_b x + log_b y

quiz.q: Which expression is equivalent to log(x/y)?
options: (log x)/(log y)
log x - log y
log x + log y
log x · log y

quiz.q: Simplify log(a^5).
options: 5 log a
log a + 5
5/log a
(log a)^5

quiz.q: Given log 2 ≈ 0.301 and log 3 ≈ 0.477, what is log 6?
Fully expand log( x²y / z³ ) using the laws of logarithms.
options: log x + log y − log z
2log x − log y − 3log z
2log x + log y + 3log z
2log x + log y − 3log z

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Curve Sketching: A Trigonometric Function Over One Period
subjects.summary: Use the first and second derivatives of a sine or cosine function to find critical points, inflection points, and concavity over a single period, tying calculus to the familiar wave shape.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Curve Sketching: A Trigonometric Function Over One Period

quiz.q: For f(x) = sin(x) on [0, 2 pi], f'(x) = cos(x). What are the critical numbers in this interval?
options: x = 0 and x = pi
x = pi/2 only
x = pi/2 and x = 3pi/2
x = pi and x = 2pi

quiz.q: Using f''(x) = -sin(x), what is the classification of the critical point at x = pi/2 for f(x) = sin(x)?
options: Local maximum, since f'(pi/2) = cos(pi/2) = 0 confirms it directly
Local maximum, since f''(pi/2) = -sin(pi/2) = -1 < 0
Local minimum, since f''(pi/2) = -1 < 0
Inflection point, since f''(pi/2) is not equal to 0

quiz.q: For f(x) = sin(x) on (0, 2 pi), f''(x) = -sin(x). At which interior x-value does f''(x) = 0 with a change in concavity, giving an inflection point?
options: x = pi/2
x = 3pi/2
x = pi/4
x = pi

quiz.q: On the interval (pi, 2 pi), what is the concavity of f(x) = sin(x)?
options: Concave down, since the function is decreasing at the start of this interval
Concave down, since f''(x) = -sin(x) > 0 there
Concave up, since f''(x) = -sin(x) > 0 there (sin(x) < 0 on this interval)
Concave up, since f(x) = sin(x) itself is negative on this interval

quiz.q: For g(x) = cos(x) on [0, 2 pi], g'(x) = -sin(x) and g''(x) = -cos(x). What is the classification of the critical point at x = pi?
options: Inflection point, since g''(x) = -cos(x) changes sign near x = pi
Local maximum, since g''(pi) = 1 > 0
Local minimum, since g''(pi) = -cos(pi) = 1 > 0
Neither a local max nor a local min, since g'(x) = -sin(x) does not actually equal zero at x = pi

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Circular Motion and Gravitation
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Physics strand: an object in circular motion experiences a centripetal force directed toward the centre of the circle, and gravitation describes the attractive force between objects with mass.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Physics: Circular Motion and Gravitation

quiz.q: Centripetal force in circular motion is directed ___.
options: Away from the centre of the circle
Toward the centre of the circle
In a direction unrelated to the object’s motion
In a straight line with no connection to the circle

quiz.q: Gravitation describes the attractive force between ___.
options: Objects with mass
Only objects with no mass
A force unrelated to mass
Objects that repel each other, never attract

quiz.q: Why does an object moving in a circular path require a continuous centripetal force?
options: Circular motion requires no force to be maintained
Objects naturally curve without any applied force
Centripetal force has no connection to circular motion
Without it, the object would move in a straight line rather than curve around the circle

quiz.q: Which is an example of circular motion influenced by gravitation?
options: An object at complete rest with no motion
A planet orbiting the Sun
A ball rolling in a straight line on flat ground
A situation with no connection to gravity

quiz.q: Why is understanding gravitation important for explaining planetary orbits?
options: Gravitation has no connection to planetary motion
Gravitational attraction between the Sun and planets provides the force that keeps them in orbit
Planets orbit with no force acting upon them
This concept has no relevance to astronomy or physics

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Eulogy and Occasional Speech
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: a eulogy or occasional speech is written for a specific ceremonial purpose, requiring a tone appropriate to the occasion and language that connects personal reflection to broader, shared meaning.

quiz.q: A eulogy or occasional speech is written for a specific ___ purpose.
options: A purpose disconnected from any audience or context
Entirely unrelated to any occasion or event
Purely technical, with no ceremonial element at all
Ceremonial

quiz.q: This type of speech requires a tone that is appropriate to ___.
options: The occasion
A factor entirely unrelated to the purpose of the speech
Only the speaker’s personal preference, with no consideration of the audience
No specific context or audience whatsoever

quiz.q: Why might a eulogy connect personal reflection to broader, shared meaning?
options: It helps an audience relate the specific memories being shared to universal themes like loss, love, or legacy
Personal reflection and broader meaning are always completely unrelated in this type of speech
A eulogy should never attempt to connect with a shared audience experience
This concept has no connection to effective occasional speech writing

quiz.q: Why is understanding the specific occasion important when writing a speech like a eulogy or a wedding toast?
options: The purpose and tone required can differ significantly depending on the specific ceremonial context
The occasion has no effect on how this type of speech should be written
This concept has no connection to effective speech writing
All occasional speeches should always be written in an identical way regardless of context

quiz.q: Why might careful word choice be especially important when writing a eulogy?
options: The language needs to convey genuine emotion and respect appropriate to a sensitive and significant occasion
Word choice has no particular significance in this specific type of writing
A eulogy should always use the most casual, informal language possible
This concept has no connection to writing an effective ceremonial speech

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Functions: Symmetry -- Even, Odd, and Neither
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: a function can be classified as even, odd, or neither based on how its graph behaves under reflection, which reveals useful structural properties about the function.

quiz.q: A function can be classified as even, odd, or ___.
options: Only positive, with no other classification possible
Neither
Only negative, with no other classification possible
A category unrelated to function symmetry

quiz.q: An even function’s graph is symmetric with respect to the ___.
options: y-axis
x-axis exclusively, with no connection to the y-axis
A concept unrelated to any axis of symmetry
Origin exclusively, with no connection to the y-axis

quiz.q: An odd function’s graph is symmetric with respect to the ___.
options: y-axis exclusively, with no connection to the origin
x-axis exclusively, with no connection to the origin
Origin
A concept unrelated to any point of symmetry

quiz.q: Why might identifying a function as even or odd be useful before analyzing or graphing it further?
options: Every function must always be treated identically regardless of any symmetry it has
This classification provides no useful information about a function’s behaviour
This concept has no connection to understanding or graphing a function
It reveals a structural property that can simplify calculations or predictions about the function’s behaviour

quiz.q: Why might recognizing a function as odd be particularly useful when evaluating a definite integral over a symmetric interval?
options: This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical calculation benefit
Symmetry classification has no connection to evaluating definite integrals
An odd function’s symmetry can allow certain integrals over a symmetric interval to be simplified or determined without full calculation
Odd functions can never be integrated using any simplified method

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Logistic Growth Models
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Calculus strand: a logistic growth model describes a quantity that initially grows rapidly but slows as it approaches a maximum sustainable value, called the carrying capacity, unlike unlimited exponential growth.

quiz.q: A logistic growth model describes a quantity that initially grows rapidly but ___ as it approaches a maximum value.
options: Slows
Immediately drops to zero with no gradual change
Continues increasing at an unlimited, ever-accelerating rate
A concept unrelated to how the quantity changes over time

quiz.q: The maximum sustainable value in a logistic growth model is called the ___.
options: Initial value exclusively, with no connection to a maximum
A concept unrelated to sustainable growth
Carrying capacity
Growth rate, with no connection to a maximum value

quiz.q: Why is a logistic growth model often more realistic than a simple exponential growth model for describing a population over a long period of time?
options: This concept has no connection to how populations actually behave over time
Logistic models are always identical to purely exponential growth models
Exponential growth always provides a perfectly accurate long-term prediction for real populations
Real populations are usually limited by factors like resources, unlike the unlimited growth assumed by a purely exponential model

quiz.q: Why does a logistic growth curve have an S-shape (or sigmoid shape) when graphed?
options: This concept has no relevance to how the model is graphed or interpreted
The S-shape has no connection to how logistic growth is mathematically defined
Growth starts slowly, accelerates, and then levels off as the quantity approaches its carrying capacity
A logistic growth curve is always a perfectly straight line with no curvature

quiz.q: Why are logistic growth models useful in fields like epidemiology, such as modelling the spread of a disease within a limited population?
options: Logistic growth models have no application in epidemiology
This concept only applies to purely theoretical mathematics with no real-world use
They can realistically capture how spread initially accelerates but then slows as the population of susceptible individuals decreases
Disease spread within a population can never be modelled mathematically

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Superconductivity
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: superconductivity is a phenomenon in which certain materials, when cooled below a critical temperature, conduct electric current with zero electrical resistance.

quiz.q: Superconductivity occurs when certain materials conduct electric current with ___.
options: Resistance that increases continuously over time with no limit
Zero electrical resistance
A property entirely unrelated to electrical resistance
Extremely high electrical resistance

quiz.q: Superconductivity occurs when a material is cooled below its ___.
options: Critical temperature
Boiling point exclusively, with no connection to a critical temperature
A factor entirely unrelated to temperature
Melting point exclusively, with no connection to a critical temperature

quiz.q: Why is zero electrical resistance in a superconductor considered a significant property?
options: Zero resistance has no meaningful benefit compared to typical conductors
Ordinary conductors already have zero electrical resistance under normal conditions
It allows electric current to flow without any energy loss due to resistance, unlike ordinary conductors
This property has no connection to how electric current flows through a material

quiz.q: Which is an example of a practical application that relies on superconductivity?
options: Powerful electromagnets used in MRI machines
A technology entirely unrelated to electricity or magnetism
An application that has no connection to cooling materials
A device that requires high electrical resistance to function

quiz.q: Why does the need for extremely low temperatures currently limit the widespread practical use of many superconducting materials?
options: Temperature has no effect on whether a material exhibits superconductivity
Maintaining such low temperatures requires significant energy and specialized equipment, adding cost and complexity
This concept has no connection to the practical challenges of using superconductors
Superconducting materials can maintain their properties at any temperature with no special conditions required

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: The TED-Style Talk
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: a TED-style talk presents a single compelling idea within a concise time limit, combining a personal narrative hook, clear structure, and a memorable closing to leave a lasting impression on the audience.

quiz.q: A TED-style talk presents ___ within a concise time limit.
options: A single compelling idea
As many unrelated ideas as possible within the given time
A purely technical report with no central idea
A concept unrelated to focused, structured communication

quiz.q: Why might a TED-style talk begin with a personal narrative hook?
options: This concept has no connection to engaging an audience from the outset
This structure never appears in an effective TED-style presentation
A relatable, personal opening can quickly capture audience interest and establish an emotional connection
A personal narrative hook always weakens the impact of this type of talk

quiz.q: Why is having a clear structure especially important for a concise talk with a strict time limit?
options: A clear structure helps ensure the core idea is communicated efficiently and memorably within limited time
Structure has no effect on how well a concise talk communicates its main idea
A time limit has no influence on how a talk should be structured
This concept has no connection to effective public speaking within a constrained format

quiz.q: Why might a TED-style talk aim to end with a particularly memorable closing statement?
options: The closing statement has no particular importance in this type of talk
A memorable ending always distracts from the main message of the talk
This concept has no connection to effective persuasive or informative speaking
A strong closing can reinforce the central idea and leave a lasting impression on the audience

quiz.q: Why is focusing on a single compelling idea, rather than several unrelated ones, considered an effective approach for this speaking format?
options: A single focused idea is easier for an audience to understand, remember, and be moved by within a short time frame
This concept has no connection to how audiences process and retain information
Focusing on a single idea always makes a talk less interesting to an audience
Multiple unrelated ideas are always more effective than a single focused one

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Recursive Sequences: Advanced Applications
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: advanced recursive sequences apply a defining rule repeatedly to model complex real-world processes, such as compound growth patterns that depend on more than one previous term.

quiz.q: Advanced recursive sequences apply a defining rule repeatedly to model ___.
options: A concept entirely unrelated to real-world modelling
Complex real-world processes
Only purely abstract patterns with no practical application
A single, isolated calculation with no repeated process involved

quiz.q: Some advanced recursive sequences depend on ___ previous term(s).
options: More than one
Only a single previous term, in every possible case
A concept unrelated to how recursive sequences are defined
Exactly zero, with no dependence on any prior term

quiz.q: Which is an example of a sequence where each term depends on the two previous terms?
options: A sequence unrelated to recursive definitions
A sequence with no defined recursive pattern whatsoever
The Fibonacci sequence
Any sequence with a constant, unchanging value throughout

quiz.q: Why might a recursive sequence be a natural way to model a population that grows based on both current and previous population data?
options: Population growth can never depend on more than a single prior data point
This concept has no connection to how recursive sequences function
Recursive sequences have no useful application for modelling population growth
A recursive definition can directly capture how a term’s value depends on one or more earlier terms in the sequence

quiz.q: Why are advanced recursive sequences relevant to computer science, particularly in the design of certain algorithms?
options: Computer science algorithms never rely on any form of recursive structure
This concept only applies to purely theoretical mathematics with no application to computing
Recursive sequences have no connection to how algorithms are designed
Many algorithms are designed using a recursive structure, where a solution depends on solutions to smaller, related instances of the same problem

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Curve Sketching: Using Sign Charts to Determine Concavity
subjects.summary: Build a sign chart for f''(x) by testing a value in each interval between its zeros (and any points where f is undefined) to determine where a function is concave up or concave down.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Curve Sketching: Using Sign Charts to Determine Concavity

quiz.q: For f(x) = x^4 - 6x^2, f''(x) = 12x^2 - 12. Which intervals make up the correct concavity sign chart?
options: Concave up everywhere except exactly at x = -1 and x = 1
Concave up on (negative infinity, -1) and (1, infinity); concave down on (-1, 1)
Concave up on (negative infinity, 0) and concave down on (0, infinity), based on the sign of x alone
Concave down on (negative infinity, -1) and (1, infinity); concave up on (-1, 1)

quiz.q: Building a sign chart for g''(x) = 6x - 24, where g(x) = x^3 - 12x^2 + 20x, which of the following is correct?
options: Concave down on (negative infinity, 24), concave up on (24, infinity)
Concave up on (negative infinity, 4), concave down on (4, infinity)
Concave down on (negative infinity, 4), concave up on (4, infinity)
Concave up everywhere, since g''(x) = 6x - 24 is a straight line

quiz.q: For k(x) = 1/(x-1), k''(x) = 2/(x-1)^3 changes sign at x = 1. Why is x = 1 NOT an inflection point of k(x)?
options: Because k(x) is undefined at x = 1 (there's a vertical asymptote there, not a point on the graph)
Because k'(x) = -1/(x-1)^2 is always negative, so k is always decreasing and can't have an inflection point
Because concavity only changes at critical numbers, and x = 1 is not a critical number of k(x)
Because k''(x) never actually equals zero at x = 1, only changes sign

quiz.q: What is the concavity of k(x) = 1/(x-1) on the interval x < 1?
options: Concave down, since k(x) itself is negative for x < 1
Concave down, since k''(x) = 2/(x-1)^3 < 0 there
Concave up, since k''(x) = 2/(x-1)^3 < 0 there
Undefined, since a sign chart cannot be built across a point of discontinuity

quiz.q: For n(x) = 3x^4 - 4x^3, n''(x) = 12x(3x - 2). Which sign chart correctly describes the concavity of n(x)?
options: Concave up on (negative infinity, 2/3) and concave down on (2/3, infinity) only
Concave up on (negative infinity, 0), concave down on (0, 2/3), concave up on (2/3, infinity)
Concave down on (negative infinity, 0), concave up on (0, 2/3), concave down on (2/3, infinity)
Concave down on (negative infinity, 0) and (2/3, infinity), concave up only exactly at x = 2/3

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Resonance and Acoustics
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: resonance occurs when a system is driven to oscillate at its natural frequency with increased amplitude, a principle central to acoustics and the design of musical instruments.

quiz.q: Resonance occurs when a system is driven to oscillate at its ___ with increased amplitude.
options: Natural frequency
A concept unrelated to oscillation
Slowest possible frequency, regardless of its natural properties
Maximum possible temperature

quiz.q: Resonance is a principle central to ___ and the design of musical instruments.
options: Only visual art, with no connection to sound
A field entirely unrelated to sound
Acoustics
A concept unrelated to oscillating systems

quiz.q: Why might a wine glass shatter when exposed to a sound at exactly its natural frequency?
options: Resonance has no effect on the vibration of a physical object like a glass
Sound waves never have any physical effect on solid objects
The resonant vibration can build up amplitude until it exceeds the structural limits of the glass
This concept has no connection to how resonance and vibration function

quiz.q: Why do musical instrument designers carefully consider the shape and material of an instrument’s body?
options: The shape and material of an instrument have no effect on the sound it produces
Resonance has no connection to how musical instruments are designed
This concept has no relevance to acoustics or instrument design
These factors influence the instrument’s resonant properties, shaping the sound quality it produces

quiz.q: Why is understanding resonance important for engineers designing structures like bridges?
options: Structures need to be designed to avoid dangerous resonant vibrations caused by factors like wind or foot traffic
This concept has no connection to structural safety or engineering design
Resonance has no relevance to the structural design of bridges or buildings
Engineers never need to consider natural frequency when designing large structures

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: Finding Your Voice -- Spoken Word and Poetry Performance
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: spoken word poetry brings a poem to life through performance, using rhythm, tone, and body language to amplify a poet's distinct voice and turn written words into a lived, embodied experience for an audience.

quiz.q: Spoken word poetry is distinct from poetry on the page because it is primarily experienced through ___.
options: A textbook with no audience
Live performance and voice
Silent reading only

options: Rhythm, tone, and body language
Footnotes and citations only
A completely monotone, unchanging voice
Elements with no connection to the poem's meaning

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose to perform a piece rather than simply publish it in written form?
options: Performance adds no new dimension to a poem's meaning
To use their voice and presence to intensify the audience's emotional connection to the words
Written poetry is always more powerful than performed poetry
Spoken word has no connection to poetic tradition

quiz.q: A poet's 'voice' in this context refers to ___.
options: Only the literal volume of their speaking voice
A quality unrelated to word choice or delivery
A concept with no relevance to poetry
Their distinctive way of expressing ideas through language, tone, and delivery

quiz.q: Why is spoken word poetry often considered a bridge between literary and oral traditions?
options: It has no connection to either literary or oral traditions
Oral tradition and written literature have never intersected
It combines the crafted language of written poetry with the immediacy of live oral performance
Spoken word poetry is unrelated to any tradition of storytelling

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Review: Logarithmic Growth, Complex Numbers, and Optimization
subjects.summary: This review covers Days 41 to 47: modelling exponential growth and decay using logarithms, iteration and fixed points of functions, the polar form of complex numbers, limits and convergence of sequences, the laws of logarithms, even/odd function symmetry, and recursive sequence applications.

quiz.q: A bacteria culture grows according to N(t) = 200(2)^(t/3), t in hours. Using logarithms, how many hours does it take to reach 1600?
options: 24 hours
6 hours
9 hours
4.5 hours

quiz.q: A complex number in polar form is expressed using magnitude and ___.
options: A factor entirely unrelated to magnitude
Colour, with no connection to complex numbers
Angle
Only its real component, with no angle involved

quiz.q: Constrained optimization involves finding a maximum or minimum value while satisfying ___.
options: A concept entirely unrelated to limiting factors
One or more limiting conditions
No conditions whatsoever
Only conditions involving a single variable, with no others considered

quiz.q: An even function’s graph is symmetric with respect to the ___.
options: Origin exclusively, with no connection to the y-axis
y-axis
A concept unrelated to any axis of symmetry
x-axis exclusively, with no connection to the y-axis

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review logarithmic growth, complex numbers, and optimization together?
options: Review is never useful in math
These topics have no connection to each other
Each topic must be learned in complete isolation
These related math concepts reinforce each other for stronger overall understanding

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Curve Sketching: Matching a Function's Graph to Its Derivative's Graph
subjects.summary: Practice reading key features of a function's graph -- increasing/decreasing behaviour, turning points, and concavity changes -- and match them to the corresponding features on the graph of its derivative.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Curve Sketching: Matching a Function's Graph to Its Derivative's Graph

quiz.q: A function f(x) is decreasing on (negative infinity, -1), increasing on (-1, 2), and decreasing on (2, infinity), with turning points at x = -1 and x = 2. Which description matches the graph of f'(x)?
options: f'(x) has turning points at x = -1 and x = 2, matching f's turning points exactly
f'(x) is negative on (negative infinity, -1), positive on (-1, 2), negative on (2, infinity), crossing the x-axis at x = -1 and x = 2
f'(x) is positive on (negative infinity, -1), negative on (-1, 2), positive on (2, infinity)
f'(x) is zero on the entire interval (-1, 2), since f is increasing throughout that interval

quiz.q: For g(x), which is concave down on (negative infinity, 0) and concave up on (0, infinity) with an inflection point at x = 0, what is true about the graph of g'(x)?
options: g'(x) is increasing on (negative infinity, 0) and decreasing on (0, infinity), so g' has a local maximum at x = 0
g'(x) has an inflection point at x = 0, matching g's inflection point
g'(x) is decreasing on (negative infinity, 0) and increasing on (0, infinity), so g' has a local minimum at x = 0
g'(x) is zero for all x < 0 and positive for all x > 0

quiz.q: If the graph of f'(x) is a straight line that is negative for x < 3, zero at x = 3, and positive for x > 3, what does this tell you about f(x)?
options: f has a local maximum at x = 3, and f is concave down everywhere
f is concave up for x < 3 and concave down for x > 3, since f'(x) changes from negative to positive
f has an inflection point at x = 3, since f'(x) = 0 there
f has a local minimum at x = 3, and f is concave up everywhere, since f''(x) is a positive constant

quiz.q: The graph of h'(x) is an upward-opening parabola with vertex at (2, 3), meaning h'(x) is greater than or equal to 3 for all x. What does this tell you about h(x)?
options: h(x) has a local minimum at x = 2, since the vertex of h'(x) occurs there
h(x) is increasing for all real x, since h'(x) is always positive and never equal to zero
h(x) is decreasing for all real x, since h'(x) is at its lowest point of 3 at the vertex
h(x) is concave up for x < 2 and concave down for x > 2, matching the parabola's own shape

quiz.q: The graph of p'(x) crosses or touches the x-axis at x = -2 (sign change + to -), x = 0 (touches zero but stays negative on both sides), and x = 3 (sign change - to +). Which correctly classifies all three critical points of p(x)?
options: Local minimum at x = -2, local maximum at x = 0, local minimum at x = 3
Local maximum at x = -2, neither max nor min at x = 0, local minimum at x = 3
All three are local maxima, since p'(x) equals zero at each
Local maximum at x = -2, local minimum at x = 0, local minimum at x = 3

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Satellites and Orbital Mechanics

A factor entirely unrelated to orbital mechanics
Internal temperature, with no connection to motion
Complete lack of any motion whatsoever

quiz.q: Orbital mechanics helps determine factors like orbital period and ___.

Colour, with no connection to a satellite’s orbit
Altitude

All satellites, regardless of altitude, always have exactly the same orbital period
This concept has no connection to how orbital mechanics functions

quiz.q: Why is precise calculation important when placing a satellite into a stable orbit?
options: This concept has no relevance to the practical challenges of satellite deployment
Even small errors in velocity or altitude can prevent a satellite from maintaining a stable, sustained orbit
Precision has no effect on whether a satellite can maintain a stable orbit

quiz.q: Why is understanding orbital mechanics essential for planning communication and weather satellite networks?
options: It ensures satellites are placed at altitudes and orbits appropriate for their specific intended function
Communication and weather satellites never require any specific orbital placement

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: Synthesizing Multiple Sources in Academic Argument
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: synthesizing multiple sources involves weaving together evidence and ideas from several texts to construct a cohesive, original argument, rather than simply summarizing each source in isolation.

quiz.q: Synthesizing multiple sources involves weaving together evidence and ideas from several texts to construct ___.

subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: electromagnetic waves consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields that travel through space, and the electromagnetic spectrum organizes these waves by wavelength and frequency, from radio waves to gamma rays.

quiz.q: Electromagnetic waves consist of oscillating electric and ___ fields.
options: Nuclear, with no connection to oscillating fields
A concept unrelated to electromagnetic waves
Gravitational, with no connection to electric fields
Magnetic

quiz.q: The electromagnetic spectrum organizes waves by wavelength and ___.
options: Mass, which electromagnetic waves do not possess
Colour exclusively, with no connection to any other property
A concept unrelated to the electromagnetic spectrum
Frequency

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of electromagnetic radiation with a very short wavelength?
options: Sound waves, which are not electromagnetic at all
Gamma rays
A type of radiation unrelated to the electromagnetic spectrum
Radio waves, which have very long wavelengths

quiz.q: Why do all types of electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum, despite having different wavelengths and frequencies?
options: The speed of light in a vacuum is a fundamental constant that applies to all electromagnetic radiation, regardless of wavelength
This concept has no connection to how electromagnetic waves behave
The speed of electromagnetic waves has no defined relationship to physical constants
Different types of electromagnetic waves always travel at significantly different speeds in a vacuum

quiz.q: Why is understanding the electromagnetic spectrum important for technologies like medical imaging and wireless communication?
options: The electromagnetic spectrum has no connection to modern technology
All parts of the electromagnetic spectrum behave identically for every possible application
Different parts of the spectrum have distinct properties that make them suited to specific practical applications
This concept has no relevance to medical imaging or communication technology

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Analyzing Deepfakes and Synthetic Media
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: deepfakes and other forms of synthetic media use artificial intelligence to create convincingly fabricated images, audio, or video, raising urgent questions about trust, authenticity, and critical media evaluation.

quiz.q: Deepfakes and synthetic media use artificial intelligence to create convincingly fabricated ___.
options: Images, audio, or video
A concept unrelated to media technology
Content that is always clearly and obviously fake to any viewer
Only printed text, with no visual or audio component

quiz.q: The rise of synthetic media raises urgent questions about trust and ___.
options: Printing costs exclusively, with no connection to content itself
File size, with no connection to the truthfulness of content
A concept entirely unrelated to how media is evaluated
Authenticity

quiz.q: Which is an example of a strategy for evaluating whether media might be a deepfake?
options: Assuming every video encountered online is automatically authentic
Ignoring the context in which the media was shared
Checking for a credible original source or cross-referencing with other reporting
A strategy entirely unrelated to evaluating synthetic media

quiz.q: Why might deepfakes pose a significant challenge to how people evaluate the credibility of visual evidence?
options: Deepfakes never appear convincing enough to be mistaken for real footage
Visual evidence has no connection to how people evaluate credibility
This concept has no relevance to media literacy or critical evaluation
They can convincingly mimic real people and events, undermining the assumption that seeing is the same as verifying

quiz.q: Why is developing skills to critically evaluate synthetic media especially important for students today?
options: This concept has no relevance to contemporary media literacy education
Synthetic media has no real-world consequences worth understanding
As this technology becomes more accessible and realistic, distinguishing authentic from fabricated media is increasingly essential for informed citizenship
These evaluation skills have no connection to being an informed member of society

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Rational Root Theorem and Polynomial Root-Finding
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: the Rational Root Theorem lists the possible rational roots of a polynomial with integer coefficients, narrowing the search when factoring or solving higher-degree polynomial equations.

quiz.q: The Rational Root Theorem lists the possible ___ of a polynomial with integer coefficients.
options: A concept unrelated to polynomial equations
Complex, non-real roots exclusively
Rational roots
Irrational roots exclusively, with no connection to rational values

quiz.q: The Rational Root Theorem is especially useful for narrowing the search when factoring or solving ___ polynomial equations.
options: Higher-degree
A concept unrelated to solving polynomial equations
Only first-degree, linear equations
Equations with no variable terms whatsoever

quiz.q: According to the Rational Root Theorem, a possible rational root is formed by dividing a factor of the constant term by a factor of the ___.
options: Exponent of the variable, with no connection to any coefficient
Number of terms in the polynomial exclusively
A concept unrelated to the Rational Root Theorem
Leading coefficient

quiz.q: Why is testing possible rational roots a practical first step when trying to factor a higher-degree polynomial by hand?
options: Every polynomial always has the same set of rational roots, regardless of its coefficients
Testing possible rational roots never helps narrow the search for actual roots
It narrows an otherwise unlimited search down to a specific, finite list of candidates worth testing
This concept has no connection to factoring higher-degree polynomials

quiz.q: Why might the Rational Root Theorem sometimes fail to identify any actual roots of a given polynomial?
options: This theorem always identifies every root of any given polynomial without exception
Every polynomial with integer coefficients is guaranteed to have at least one rational root
This concept has no connection to the nature of a polynomial’s actual roots
A polynomial with integer coefficients can have roots that are irrational or complex rather than rational

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Calculus: Newton’s Method for Root Approximation
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Calculus strand: Newton’s Method uses a function’s tangent lines to iteratively generate closer and closer approximations to a root, starting from an initial guess and refining it using the function’s derivative.

quiz.q: Newton’s Method uses a function’s tangent lines to iteratively generate closer approximations to a ___.
options: Root
Constant term, with no connection to solving the equation
Local maximum exclusively, with no connection to roots
A concept unrelated to approximating a function’s behaviour

quiz.q: Newton’s Method begins with an initial guess and refines it using the function’s ___.
options: A concept unrelated to Newton’s Method
Constant term only, with no derivative involved
Derivative
Second antiderivative exclusively

quiz.q: Each iteration of Newton’s Method typically produces an approximation that is ___ to the actual root than the previous one.
options: Farther from
A concept unrelated to how Newton’s Method works
Exactly identical, with no meaningful change from the previous approximation
Closer

quiz.q: Why might Newton’s Method be preferred over algebraic factoring when solving certain equations?
options: Algebraic factoring can always solve any equation exactly, making other methods unnecessary
Newton’s Method is always slower and less accurate than algebraic factoring for every possible equation
Many equations, such as those involving transcendental functions, cannot be solved exactly using algebraic factoring alone
This concept has no connection to solving equations that resist algebraic methods

quiz.q: Why is a poor initial guess sometimes a problem when applying Newton’s Method?
options: The initial guess has no effect on whether Newton’s Method successfully converges to a root
Newton’s Method always converges correctly and quickly, regardless of the initial guess chosen
This concept has no relevance to the practical application of Newton’s Method
A poor starting guess can cause the sequence of approximations to converge slowly, to the wrong root, or fail to converge at all

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Neutron Stars and Stellar Remnants
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: a neutron star is an extremely dense stellar remnant formed when a massive star’s core collapses after a supernova, packing roughly the mass of the Sun into a sphere only a few kilometres across.

quiz.q: A neutron star is an extremely dense stellar remnant formed when a massive star’s core collapses after a ___.
options: Supernova
A minor, gradual cooling process with no dramatic collapse
A concept unrelated to the life cycle of a star
A completely stable, unchanging period with no collapse involved

quiz.q: A neutron star packs roughly the mass of the Sun into a sphere only a few ___ across.
options: Millimetres, an enormously smaller distance
Light-years, an enormously larger distance
A unit entirely unrelated to describing a neutron star’s size
Kilometres

quiz.q: Neutron stars are primarily composed of tightly packed ___.
options: Empty space, with no particles present at all
Free electrons exclusively, with no other particles present
A type of particle unrelated to neutron star composition
Neutrons

quiz.q: Why does a neutron star’s extreme density result in such an intense gravitational field at its surface?
options: Gravitational field strength is always identical for every type of stellar remnant
This concept has no relevance to understanding the physics of neutron stars
Gravitational field strength depends on how much mass is concentrated within a given volume, and a neutron star packs enormous mass into a very small space
A neutron star’s density has no connection to the strength of its gravitational field

quiz.q: Why do astrophysicists study neutron stars to test predictions of general relativity?
options: Neutron stars have no connection to testing theories of gravity
Their extreme density and gravity create conditions where relativistic effects become especially pronounced and measurable
General relativity makes no distinctive predictions about extremely dense objects
This concept has no relevance to modern astrophysics research

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: Diasporic Identity and Migration Narratives
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: diasporic literature explores the experiences of individuals and communities living away from an ancestral homeland, often examining themes of displacement, hybrid identity, and the tension between memory and belonging.

quiz.q: Diasporic literature explores the experiences of individuals and communities living away from an ___.
options: Ancestral homeland
Empty, unpopulated location with no cultural history
Entirely fictional setting with no connection to any real place
A concept unrelated to migration or identity

quiz.q: Diasporic literature often examines themes of displacement and ___ identity.
options: A concept unrelated to diasporic experience
Hybrid
Completely erased, with no cultural connection remaining
Entirely singular, with no blending of cultural influences

quiz.q: A recurring tension in diasporic narratives is often between memory and ___.
options: A concept entirely unrelated to identity or place
Only geography, with no connection to a character’s inner life
Financial success exclusively, with no connection to identity
Belonging

quiz.q: Why might a diasporic narrative depict a character navigating two or more distinct cultural worlds?
options: Diasporic narratives never depict characters engaging with more than one culture
This reflects the lived reality of many diasporic individuals, who often draw on and reconcile multiple cultural influences
This concept has no connection to how diasporic identity is portrayed in literature
Cultural influence has no relevance to a character’s sense of identity

quiz.q: Why is diasporic literature an important area of study within a broader survey of contemporary world literature?
options: Migration and displacement are not meaningful subjects for literary exploration
Diasporic literature has no connection to broader patterns in contemporary world literature
This concept has no relevance to studying literature from a global perspective
It offers vital perspectives on migration, identity, and belonging that reflect significant global realities

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Statistics: The Normal Distribution and Z-Scores
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: the normal distribution is a symmetric, bell-shaped probability distribution describing many real-world data sets, and a z-score expresses how many standard deviations a value lies from the mean.

quiz.q: The normal distribution is a symmetric, ___ probability distribution.
options: A concept unrelated to probability distributions
Bell-shaped
Rectangular, with equal probability across the entire range
Sharply spiked at only a single possible value

quiz.q: A z-score expresses how many standard deviations a value lies from the ___.
options: Total number of data points collected
Minimum possible value in the entire data set
Mean
A concept unrelated to standard deviation

quiz.q: In a normal distribution, most data values cluster ___ the mean.
options: Close to
A concept unrelated to how a normal distribution is shaped
Extremely far from, with almost no values near it
Exclusively at, with no values anywhere else

quiz.q: Why is a z-score useful for comparing values that come from data sets with different means and standard deviations?
options: A z-score standardizes a value, expressing its relative position within its own distribution so different data sets can be meaningfully compared
This concept has no relevance to comparing data across different distributions
A z-score has no connection to how far a value lies from its data set’s mean
Z-scores can never be used to compare values from different data sets

quiz.q: Why is the normal distribution considered a foundational model in statistics, appearing in fields from psychology to quality control?
options: This concept has no relevance to fields outside of mathematics
Real-world data sets never resemble a bell-shaped distribution
The normal distribution has no practical application outside of pure mathematics
Many natural and measured phenomena approximately follow this bell-shaped pattern, making it broadly applicable for analysis and prediction

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Calculus: Hyperbolic Functions and Their Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Calculus strand: hyperbolic functions, such as sinh(x) and cosh(x), are defined using combinations of exponential functions and share structural similarities with trigonometric functions, including distinct derivative rules.

quiz.q: Hyperbolic functions, such as sinh(x) and cosh(x), are defined using combinations of ___ functions.
options: Purely constant functions, with no variable component
Exponential
Logarithmic functions exclusively, with no connection to exponentials
A concept unrelated to how hyperbolic functions are defined

quiz.q: Hyperbolic functions share structural similarities with ___ functions, including distinct derivative rules.
options: Rational functions exclusively, with no other similarity
Only linear functions, with no other connection
A category of functions entirely unrelated to hyperbolic functions
Trigonometric

quiz.q: The derivative of cosh(x) is ___.
options: Sinh(x)
Cosh(x), identical to the original function
Negative sinh(x), the opposite sign
A result entirely unrelated to hyperbolic function derivatives

quiz.q: Why might hyperbolic functions be useful for describing the shape of a hanging cable or chain?
options: Hyperbolic functions have no application in modelling physical shapes like a hanging cable
This concept has no connection to real-world applications of calculus
A hanging cable’s shape can never be described using any mathematical function
The curve formed by a hanging cable, called a catenary, can be precisely modelled using the cosh function

quiz.q: Why is understanding hyperbolic functions valuable preparation for further study in calculus and physics?
options: Hyperbolic functions have no further application beyond an introductory Grade 12 calculus course
This concept has no relevance to further mathematical or scientific study
These functions never appear in any physics or engineering context
They appear in contexts ranging from special relativity to engineering, and their derivative rules parallel those of trigonometric functions

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Nuclear Binding Energy and Mass Defect
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: the mass defect of a nucleus is the difference between the total mass of its separate protons and neutrons and the actual mass of the bound nucleus, and this missing mass corresponds to the nucleus’s binding energy.

quiz.q: The mass defect of a nucleus is the difference between the total mass of its separate protons and neutrons and the actual mass of the ___.
options: Bound nucleus
Surrounding electron cloud exclusively, with no connection to the nucleus
A concept unrelated to nuclear structure
Entire atom’s outermost electron shell only

quiz.q: The missing mass in a nucleus corresponds to its ___.
options: Binding energy
A concept unrelated to nuclear stability
Electric charge exclusively, with no connection to energy
Total number of protons, with no connection to energy

quiz.q: Binding energy can be understood using Einstein’s famous relationship between ___.
options: Mass and energy
A concept unrelated to nuclear physics
Force and acceleration exclusively, with no connection to mass or energy
Voltage and current, with no connection to nuclear structure

quiz.q: Why does a nucleus with a larger binding energy per nucleon tend to be more stable?
options: Binding energy per nucleon has no connection to how stable a nucleus is
This concept has no relevance to understanding nuclear stability
A larger binding energy per nucleon always makes a nucleus less stable
A greater binding energy per nucleon means more energy would be required to break the nucleus apart into its individual particles

quiz.q: Why is the concept of mass defect and binding energy essential to understanding both nuclear fission and fusion?
options: Both processes release energy because the resulting nuclei have a different total binding energy than the starting nuclei
Mass defect and binding energy have no connection to how fission or fusion release energy
Fission and fusion release energy through a process entirely unrelated to nuclear mass or binding
This concept has no relevance to understanding nuclear reactions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Academic Book Review
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: an academic book review summarizes a text’s central argument, evaluates its evidence and methodology, and situates the work within a broader field of scholarship, going beyond a simple opinion or summary.

quiz.q: An academic book review summarizes a text’s central ___.
options: Cover design and page count exclusively
Author’s personal biography only, with no connection to the text’s content
Argument
A concept unrelated to reviewing a text

quiz.q: An academic book review evaluates a text’s evidence and ___.
options: A concept unrelated to academic evaluation
Number of chapters exclusively, with no connection to content
Font choice, with no connection to the quality of the work
Methodology

quiz.q: An academic book review situates a work within a broader field of ___.
options: Scholarship
Unrelated entertainment media exclusively
A concept entirely unrelated to how a text connects to other work
The author’s personal finances

quiz.q: Why does an academic book review go beyond a simple summary or personal opinion of a text?
options: It critically assesses the strength of the argument and evidence, offering an informed evaluation grounded in the wider field
This concept has no connection to how academic texts are assessed
Critical evaluation has no role in this type of writing
An academic book review is identical in every way to a simple personal opinion

quiz.q: Why is writing an academic book review considered valuable preparation for university-level coursework?
options: It builds skills in critical reading, evaluating evidence, and engaging with existing scholarship, all central to academic writing
Academic book reviews require no critical thinking or evaluation skills
This concept has no relevance to preparing for post-secondary academic work
This type of writing has no connection to skills needed in university coursework

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Function Notation: Analyzing Piecewise-Defined Functions
subjects.summary: Practice evaluating piecewise-defined functions using function notation, determining which piece applies for a given input based on its domain restriction, and checking whether the pieces connect continuously at the boundary.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Function Notation: Analyzing Piecewise-Defined Functions

quiz.q: Given f(x) = { x^2 - 3x, if x < 4 ; 2x + 1, if x ≥ 4 }, evaluate f(4).
Using the same f(x) = { x^2 - 3x, if x < 4 ; 2x + 1, if x ≥ 4 }, evaluate f(2).
For f(x) = { x^2 - 3x, if x < 4 ; 2x + 1, if x ≥ 4 }, what is the domain restriction on the piece 2x + 1?
For f(x) = { x^2 - 3x, if x < 4 ; 2x + 1, if x ≥ 4 }, is f continuous at x = 4?
options: No, because the two pieces give different values at the boundary (4 vs. 9)
Yes, because x = 4 is included in the second piece's domain
No, because the two pieces have different degrees
Yes, because both pieces are defined for all real numbers

quiz.q: For f(x) = { x^2 - 3x, if x < 4 ; 2x + 1, if x ≥ 4 }, what is f(0) + f(5)?

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Optimization: Maximizing the Area of a Norman Window
subjects.summary: A Norman window is a rectangle topped by a semicircle, and a carpenter has exactly 20 ft of trim to frame its outer edge — find the rectangle's width and height that let in the maximum amount of light (maximum total area).
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Optimization: Maximizing the Area of a Norman Window

quiz.q: Let x be the width of the rectangle (also the diameter of the semicircle on top) and h be the height of the rectangular part. The trim covers the bottom, two sides, and the semicircular arc (not the straight top, since the semicircle sits there). Which equation gives the total trim length P = 20?
options: x + 2h + πx = 20

quiz.q: Solving the trim constraint for h gives h = (20 − x − πx/2)/2. The total area (rectangle plus semicircle) is A = xh + π(x/2)²/1, i.e., A = xh + πx²/8. After substituting h, A(x) simplifies to which form?
What is A'(x) for A(x) = 10x − x²(1/2 + π/8)?
Solving A'(x) = 0 gives x = 40/(4 + π), which is approximately:
At x ≈ 5.60 ft, the height works out to h ≈ 2.80 ft (exactly half of x). What is the maximum total area of the window, to the nearest tenth?
options: A ≈ 28.0 ft²
A ≈ 40.0 ft²
A ≈ 15.7 ft²
A ≈ 22.4 ft²

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Lenses and Optical Instruments (Telescopes and Microscopes)
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: lenses refract light to form images, and combining multiple lenses in optical instruments like telescopes and microscopes can magnify distant or tiny objects beyond what a single lens could achieve.

quiz.q: Lenses form images by ___ light.
options: Reflecting exclusively, with no refraction involved
A concept unrelated to how lenses function
Refracting
Completely absorbing, with no light passing through

quiz.q: Combining multiple lenses in optical instruments can ___ distant or tiny objects beyond what a single lens could achieve.
options: Magnify
Completely hide from view, with no image produced
A concept unrelated to optical instruments
Shrink to an unusable, indistinguishable size

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of an optical instrument that uses combined lenses to view distant objects?
options: A telescope
A mirror with no lens involved at all
A device entirely unrelated to viewing distant objects
A flashlight, which produces light rather than forming an image

quiz.q: Why does a microscope typically use two separate lenses, an objective lens and an eyepiece, rather than a single lens?
options: A microscope’s design has no connection to how its lenses work together
Combining two lenses allows the image formed by the first lens to be magnified further by the second, achieving much greater overall magnification
This concept has no relevance to how optical instruments achieve magnification
Using two lenses always produces exactly the same magnification as using only one

quiz.q: Why is understanding lens behaviour important for designing optical instruments used in scientific research, such as advanced telescopes?
options: Lens behaviour has no connection to the design of scientific optical instruments
This concept has no relevance to producing clear, magnified images
Precisely controlling how lenses refract and focus light is essential for achieving clear, accurately magnified images
Optical instruments used in research never rely on any understanding of lenses

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: Facilitating a Panel Discussion
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: facilitating a panel discussion involves guiding multiple speakers through a structured conversation, balancing airtime, asking clarifying questions, and keeping the discussion focused on its central topic.

quiz.q: Facilitating a panel discussion involves guiding multiple speakers through a ___ conversation.
options: Completely unplanned, with no guidance from a facilitator
A concept unrelated to oral communication
Silent, with no spoken conversation at all
Structured

quiz.q: A skilled facilitator balances ___ among panelists.
options: A concept unrelated to facilitating group discussion
Only the opinions of a single panelist, ignoring all others
Background noise, with no connection to speaker participation
Airtime

quiz.q: A facilitator often asks ___ questions to help the audience better understand a panelist’s point.
options: A concept unrelated to facilitating discussion
Deliberately confusing, with no intent to aid understanding
Entirely unrelated, with no connection to the discussion topic
Clarifying

quiz.q: Why might a facilitator need to gently redirect a panel discussion back to its central topic?
options: This concept has no connection to effectively facilitating a group conversation
A facilitator should never attempt to guide the direction of a panel discussion
Conversations can naturally drift, and redirection helps ensure the discussion remains valuable and focused for the audience
Panel discussions never drift away from their intended topic

quiz.q: Why is facilitating a panel discussion considered a valuable oral communication skill to develop at the Grade 12 level?
options: This skill has no connection to future academic or professional communication
It requires active listening, quick thinking, and the ability to manage group dynamics, all skills valuable in academic and professional settings
This concept has no relevance to developing strong oral communication abilities
Facilitating a panel discussion requires no particular skill or preparation

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Number Theory: Modular Arithmetic and Applications
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: modular arithmetic describes a system where numbers wrap around after reaching a fixed value called the modulus, with wide applications in areas such as cryptography and scheduling.

quiz.q: Modular arithmetic describes a system where numbers wrap around after reaching a fixed value called the ___.
options: Coefficient, with no connection to how numbers wrap around
A concept unrelated to this number system
Modulus
Determinant, a concept unrelated to modular arithmetic

quiz.q: Modular arithmetic has wide applications in areas such as cryptography and ___.
options: A field entirely unrelated to any practical application
Scheduling
A concept unrelated to modular arithmetic’s uses
Only purely decorative art, with no mathematical or practical use

quiz.q: In modulo 5 arithmetic, what is 12 mod 5?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why is a standard analog clock often used as an everyday example of modular arithmetic?
options: This concept has no relevance to understanding modular systems
A clock has no connection to how modular arithmetic functions
The hours wrap back around to 1 after reaching 12, mirroring how modular arithmetic wraps around after reaching the modulus
Clocks always count upward with no repeating or wrapping pattern

quiz.q: Why is modular arithmetic considered essential to modern cryptographic systems that protect digital information?
options: Many encryption methods rely on the mathematical properties of numbers within a modular system to securely encode and decode information
Modular arithmetic has no connection to how digital information is secured
This concept has no relevance to digital security or encryption
Cryptography never relies on any mathematical structure or system

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Optimization: Minimizing the Surface Area of a Cylindrical Can
subjects.summary: An aluminum can must hold exactly 250π cm³ of liquid — find the radius and height that minimize the total surface area of metal used (top, bottom, and side combined).
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Optimization: Minimizing the Surface Area of a Cylindrical Can

quiz.q: For a cylinder of radius r and height h, the volume is V = πr²h = 250π. Solving for h in terms of r gives:
options: h = 250π/r²

quiz.q: The total surface area (two circular ends plus the lateral side) is S = 2πr² + 2πrh. After substituting h = 250/r², S(r) becomes:
options: S(r) = 2πr² + 250π/r
S(r) = 2πr + 500π/r
S(r) = 2πr² + 500π/r
S(r) = πr² + 500π/r

quiz.q: What is S'(r) for S(r) = 2πr² + 500π/r?
options: S'(r) = 2πr − 500π/r²
S'(r) = 4πr + 500π/r²
S'(r) = 4πr − 500π/r²

quiz.q: Setting S'(r) = 0 and solving gives r³ = 125, so:
options: r = 5 cm
r = 5π cm
r = 25 cm

quiz.q: At r = 5 cm, the height is h = 10 cm, meaning the can's height equals its diameter. What is the minimum surface area?
options: S = 100π cm²
S = 150π cm²
S = 250π cm²
S = 200π cm²

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: Simple Machines and Mechanical Advantage
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: a simple machine, such as a lever or pulley, changes the size or direction of an applied force, and its mechanical advantage describes the ratio between the output force and the input force.

quiz.q: A simple machine, such as a lever or pulley, changes the size or ___ of an applied force.
options: Direction
Colour, with no connection to how force is applied
Chemical composition, with no connection to mechanical force
A concept unrelated to simple machines

quiz.q: Mechanical advantage describes the ratio between the output force and the ___ force.
options: A completely unrelated, external force with no connection to the machine
Gravitational force exclusively, regardless of the machine involved
A concept unrelated to mechanical advantage
Input

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a simple machine?
options: A thermometer, which measures temperature rather than force
A lever
A device entirely unrelated to mechanical force
A battery, which stores electrical energy rather than transmitting mechanical force

quiz.q: Why can a lever allow a person to lift a heavy object using less applied force than lifting it directly?
options: Mechanical advantage has no connection to how a lever functions
A lever can trade a smaller input force over a greater distance for a larger output force over a shorter distance
This concept has no relevance to understanding simple machines
A lever always requires exactly the same force as lifting an object directly, with no advantage at all

quiz.q: Why do engineers consider mechanical advantage when designing tools and machines for practical tasks?
options: Understanding mechanical advantage helps engineers design tools that make physical tasks easier or more efficient to perform
Mechanical advantage has no practical relevance to designing tools or machines
This concept only applies to purely theoretical physics with no practical use
Engineers never need to consider the relationship between input and output force

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Comparing Dystopian Visions: Brave New World vs. Nineteen Eighty-Four
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: Aldous Huxley's Brave New World and George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four imagine two very different dystopias — a plastic, consumerist pleasure-state versus a surveillance state built on fear and propaganda — and comparing them reveals how each captures different anxieties about control.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Comparing Dystopian Visions: Brave New World vs. Nineteen Eighty-Four

quiz.q: Nineteen Eighty-Four imagines a dystopia primarily built on ___.
options: A concept unrelated to Orwell's novel
Government surveillance, propaganda, and control of information
Unlimited personal freedom with no government presence
A society with no leadership of any kind

quiz.q: Brave New World imagines a dystopia primarily built on ___.
options: A concept unrelated to Huxley's novel
Open rebellion against a corrupt government
Engineered pleasure, consumerism, and distraction rather than fear
The complete absence of technology

quiz.q: Why do critics often argue Nineteen Eighty-Four feels newly relevant in the era of state surveillance and 'fake news'?
options: The novel has no connection to contemporary concerns about surveillance or misinformation
Orwell's imagined control of information and truth echoes real debates about propaganda and surveillance today
This concept has no relevance to how the novel is read today
Nineteen Eighty-Four is set entirely in the past with no future-facing themes

quiz.q: Why do critics often argue Brave New World feels newly relevant in an era of consumerism and engineered distraction?
options: Huxley's vision of comfort, entertainment, and consumerism as tools of control echoes concerns about modern media and technology
The novel has no connection to modern consumer culture
This concept has no relevance to how the novel is read today
Brave New World predicted no aspect of technological or social change

quiz.q: Comparing these two dystopias helps readers understand that ___.
options: Only one vision of dystopia has ever been considered valid
Control over a society can take very different forms — through fear and force, or through comfort and distraction
Dystopian fiction has no relevance to understanding real societies
Brave New World and Nineteen Eighty-Four describe identical societies

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Functions: Rational Exponents, Radicals, and Simplification Techniques
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: rational exponents express roots and powers together in a single notation, allowing radical expressions to be simplified and manipulated using the same rules that apply to integer exponents.

options: A concept entirely unrelated to exponents or radicals
Geometric shape, with no connection to numerical expressions
Notation
Physical measurement, with no connection to algebraic notation

quiz.q: Rational exponents allow radical expressions to be simplified using the same rules that apply to ___ exponents.
options: Only negative exponents, with no connection to positive integer exponents
Integer
Undefined exponents, with no consistent rules at all
A concept unrelated to simplifying expressions

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Optimization: Minimizing the Distance from a Point to a Curve
subjects.summary: Find the point on the parabola y = x² that lies closest to the fixed point (0, 4.5), by minimizing the square of the distance between a general point on the curve and that fixed point.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Optimization: Minimizing the Distance from a Point to a Curve

quiz.q: A general point on the curve y = x² is (x, x²). The squared distance to the fixed point (0, 4.5) is D(x) = x² + (x² − 4.5)². Expanded and simplified, D(x) equals:
options: D(x) = x⁴ − 8x² + 4.5

quiz.q: Why minimize D(x) = x² + (x² − 4.5)² (squared distance) instead of the actual distance √[x² + (x² − 4.5)²] directly?
options: Squared distance avoids the square root, and it is minimized at the same x-value as the actual distance since both are non-negative
Squared distance and actual distance give different minimizing x-values, but squared distance is easier to graph
Squaring is required because distances in calculus must always be positive
The square root cannot be differentiated at all, so squaring is the only workaround

quiz.q: What is D'(x) for D(x) = x⁴ − 8x² + 20.25?
options: D'(x) = 4x³ − 8x

quiz.q: Solving 4x³ − 16x = 0 gives 4x(x² − 4) = 0, so the candidate x-values are:
options: x = 2, x = −2 only
x = 0 only

quiz.q: Testing the candidates (using the second derivative or a sign check) shows x = 0 gives a local maximum of D, while x = 2 and x = −2 both give the minimum distance. What is the closest point on y = x² to (0, 4.5), taking x = 2, and the minimum distance?
options: Point (2, 4), distance = √4.5 ≈ 2.12
Point (2, 4.5), distance = 2
Point (2, 4), distance = 4.25
Point (2, 4), distance = √4.25 ≈ 2.06

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Physics: The Uncertainty Principle and Quantum Measurement
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: the uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of properties, such as a particle’s position and momentum, cannot both be known with arbitrary precision at the same time, a fundamental limit rather than a measurement flaw.

quiz.q: The uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of properties cannot both be known with ___ at the same time.
options: A concept unrelated to measurement in quantum physics
Complete inaccuracy, with no meaningful information available at all
Any degree of precision whatsoever, under any circumstances
Arbitrary precision

quiz.q: A classic pair of properties limited by the uncertainty principle is a particle’s position and ___.
options: Colour, a property that particles at this scale do not possess
A concept unrelated to the uncertainty principle
Name, which has no physical or measurable meaning
Momentum

quiz.q: The limit described by the uncertainty principle is considered ___ rather than a flaw in measurement technique.
options: A concept unrelated to the nature of this physical limit
Completely avoidable with sufficiently advanced instruments
Irrelevant to how particles actually behave
Fundamental

quiz.q: Why does increasing the precision of a position measurement for a quantum particle necessarily increase the uncertainty in its momentum?
options: According to the uncertainty principle, the product of the uncertainties in these two properties cannot fall below a fundamental limit
Position and momentum have no established mathematical relationship at the quantum scale
Measuring position more precisely always has no effect whatsoever on how precisely momentum can be known
This concept has no relevance to how quantum measurement works

quiz.q: Why was the uncertainty principle a significant departure from the assumptions of classical physics?
options: It revealed a fundamental limit to what can be simultaneously known about a system, challenging the classical assumption of unlimited measurement precision
Classical physics already assumed inherent limits on measurement precision at every scale
The uncertainty principle made no meaningful change to how physicists understood measurement
This concept has no relevance to the historical development of quantum theory

Punctuation choices have no meaningful effect on how a reader experiences a piece of writing

options: This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical use

subjects.title: Optimization: Maximizing Revenue from a Price-Demand Function
subjects.summary: A company's price-demand model is p = 120 − 3q (price in dollars per unit if q units are sold per week) — find the number of units to sell that maximizes weekly revenue.

quiz.q: Revenue is price times quantity: R(q) = q · p = q(120 − 3q). Expanded, R(q) equals:

Setting R'(q) = 0 and solving gives:
options: q = 20 units
q = 60 units
q = 40 units
q = 10 units

quiz.q: Since R''(q) = −6 < 0 for all q, the critical point q = 20 is confirmed to be:
options: a point of inflection, not an extremum
an absolute maximum of revenue
an absolute minimum of revenue
undetermined without checking endpoints

quiz.q: At q = 20 units, what are the selling price and the maximum weekly revenue?

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Optimization: Minimizing Material for a Cone of Fixed Volume
subjects.summary: A paper cone-shaped cup (open top, no base circle, no lid) must hold about 40 cm³ — find the radius and height that minimize the amount of paper (lateral surface area) needed to make it.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Optimization: Minimizing Material for a Cone of Fixed Volume

quiz.q: For a cone of radius r and height h, the volume is V = (1/3)πr²h. If V is fixed, solving for h in terms of r and V gives:
options: h = V/(πr²)
h = 3V/(πr)
h = 3V/(πr²)
h = πr²/(3V)

quiz.q: The lateral (side) surface area of an open cone is S = πrl, where l = √(r² + h²) is the slant height. Working through the calculus of minimizing S for a fixed volume V leads to a critical point where h and r satisfy which relationship?
options: h = r√2
h = r²
h = 2r

quiz.q: Using h = r√2 together with V = (1/3)πr²h ≈ 40 cm³, what radius r (to the nearest whole cm) minimizes the paper used?
options: r = 5 cm
r = 2 cm
r = 4 cm
r = 3 cm

quiz.q: At r = 3 cm, what is the corresponding height h (to 2 decimal places)?
With r = 3 cm and h ≈ 4.24 cm, the slant height is l = √(r² + h²) = √27 ≈ 5.20 cm. What is the resulting minimum lateral surface area?
options: S ≈ 15.6 cm²
S ≈ 84.8 cm²
S ≈ 49.0 cm²
S ≈ 28.3 cm²

subjects.title: Optimization: Maximizing the Volume of a Folded Box
subjects.summary: A square sheet of cardboard measuring 24 cm by 24 cm has equal squares cut from each corner, and the flaps are folded up to form an open-top box — find the size of the cut that maximizes the box's volume.

quiz.q: If a square of side x is cut from each corner of the 24 cm × 24 cm sheet, the resulting open box has base side (24 − 2x) and height x. Which expression gives the volume V(x)?

options: x = 12 is an endpoint of the domain where the base side (24 − 2x) becomes 0, giving zero volume, not a maximum
x = 12 produces a negative volume, which is impossible
x = 12 is outside the interval where V'(x) = 0 has any solution
x = 12 makes V'(x) undefined rather than zero
