subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Non-Inertial Reference Frames and Pseudo-Forces
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: a non-inertial reference frame is one that is accelerating or rotating, and within such a frame an observer must introduce fictitious pseudo-forces, forces with no physical source, to correctly account for motion that appears to violate Newtons laws when analyzed in that accelerating frame.

quiz.q: What defines a non-inertial reference frame?
options: It is a reference frame moving at a constant velocity with no acceleration
It is a reference frame that is accelerating or rotating
It is a reference frame that is always perfectly stationary
It is a reference frame with no relationship to acceleration of any kind

quiz.q: What must an observer introduce to correctly describe motion within a non-inertial frame?
options: No forces of any kind, regardless of the frames motion
Only forces with a clearly identifiable physical source
Fictitious pseudo-forces, with no physical source
A force that always exactly cancels gravity

quiz.q: Why do pseudo-forces appear necessary when analyzing motion from within an accelerating frame?
options: Pseudo-forces are required in every reference frame, whether inertial or not
Pseudo-forces eliminate the need to ever apply Newtons laws
Newtons laws hold identically in every frame with no adjustment required
Motion that appears to violate Newtons laws in that frame can be correctly accounted for by including these extra terms

quiz.q: How does the concept of a non-inertial frame relate to the Coriolis effect, studied in an earlier batch?
options: The Coriolis effect only occurs in a perfectly inertial frame with no rotation
The Coriolis effect is a specific pseudo-force that arises for an observer within a rotating non-inertial frame, such as the rotating Earth
The Coriolis effect has no connection to non-inertial reference frames
Non-inertial frames never give rise to any observable pseudo-force effects

quiz.q: Why is understanding non-inertial frames and pseudo-forces important for analyzing motion observed from a rotating platform, such as Earth?
options: Motion observed from a rotating platform never requires any special analysis
Non-inertial frames only matter for objects that are not actually moving at all
Without accounting for these fictitious forces, motion observed from such a platform would appear to violate Newtons laws in ways otherwise unexplained
Pseudo-forces have no practical relevance to analyzing motion on Earth

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Drama: The Problem Play and Social Commentary on the Stage
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: a problem play, closely associated with dramatists such as Henrik Ibsen, uses a realistic domestic or social setting to stage a specific contemporary social issue, often leaving the conflict unresolved so that the audience is left to confront the problem rather than receive a tidy conclusion.

quiz.q: What kind of issue does a problem play typically stage?
options: A historical event from many centuries earlier with no contemporary relevance
A specific contemporary social issue, often within a realistic domestic setting
A purely fantastical conflict with no connection to real social life
A conflict resolved entirely offstage before the play begins

quiz.q: With which dramatist is the problem play especially associated?
options: A purely comic playwright with no interest in social issues
A dramatist with no connection to realistic social drama
Henrik Ibsen
A writer exclusively of ancient Greek tragedy

quiz.q: What is distinctive about how a problem play often ends?
options: The ending always ignores the social issue raised earlier
The conflict is often left unresolved, confronting the audience with the problem rather than a tidy conclusion
Every problem play ends with the issue fully and neatly resolved
Problem plays never reach any kind of ending

quiz.q: How does the problem play compare to the revenge tragedy studied in an earlier batch?
options: The two forms are identical in setting, subject, and purpose
The revenge tragedy is set in a realistic contemporary domestic household
Both use dramatic conflict to engage an audience, but the problem play stages a realistic contemporary social issue while the revenge tragedy centres on vengeance for a specific grievous wrong
The problem play always involves supernatural revenge

quiz.q: Why might leaving a problem plays central conflict unresolved be an effective dramatic choice?
options: Unresolved endings make a play impossible to stage
A problem play with an unresolved ending cannot address any social issue at all
An unresolved ending removes any possibility of audience engagement
It can provoke the audience into continued reflection and debate about the issue rather than allowing easy dismissal

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Statistics: Type I and Type II Errors in Hypothesis Testing
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: a Type I error occurs when a true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected, while a Type II error occurs when a false null hypothesis is incorrectly retained, and understanding the tradeoff between these two kinds of mistakes is central to designing and interpreting a hypothesis test.

quiz.q: What happens during a Type I error?
options: No hypothesis of any kind is being tested
A true null hypothesis is correctly retained
A false null hypothesis is correctly rejected
A true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected

quiz.q: What happens during a Type II error?
options: A false null hypothesis is correctly rejected
The sample size becomes undefined
A true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected
A false null hypothesis is incorrectly retained

quiz.q: Why is there generally a tradeoff between the risks of Type I and Type II errors?
options: Reducing the chance of one type of error, given a fixed sample size, tends to increase the chance of the other
The two types of error are always completely independent of sample design choices
Type I and Type II errors always occur together in every single test
Both types of error can always be reduced to exactly zero simultaneously

quiz.q: How does the concept of Type I and Type II errors relate to the p-value studied in an earlier batch?
options: Type I and Type II errors can only be defined without any reference to a significance threshold
A p-value always guarantees that no Type II error can occur
The chosen significance threshold for the p-value directly determines the risk of making a Type I error
The p-value has no connection whatsoever to Type I or Type II errors

quiz.q: Why is understanding both types of error important when designing a hypothesis test, such as an ANOVA studied in an earlier batch?
options: ANOVA and other hypothesis tests are immune to both types of error
It helps researchers balance the risk of falsely finding an effect against the risk of missing a real one, shaping design choices such as sample size
Understanding these errors has no bearing on how a hypothesis test is designed
A well-designed test can always guarantee zero risk of either type of error

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Algebra: Solving Systems of Nonlinear Equations
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Math strand: a system of nonlinear equations includes at least one equation that is not linear, such as a quadratic or circle equation, and can be solved using substitution or graphing, often producing more than one solution where the curves intersect.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Algebra: Solving Systems of Nonlinear Equations

quiz.q: What makes a system of equations nonlinear?
options: At least one equation in the system is not linear, such as a quadratic or circle equation
The system contains no equations at all
The system can only ever have exactly one variable
Every equation in the system must be a straight line

quiz.q: Which method can be used to solve a system of nonlinear equations?
options: Ignoring one of the equations entirely
Substitution or graphing
Randomly guessing values with no verification
Converting every equation into an unrelated word problem

quiz.q: How many solutions can a system involving a line and a circle potentially have?
options: Always exactly one solution in every possible case
Exactly three solutions with no exceptions
Zero, one, or two solutions, depending on where the curves intersect
An infinite number of solutions in every possible case

quiz.q: What does a solution to a system of nonlinear equations represent graphically?
options: The exact centre of only one of the two curves
A point where the graphs of the equations intersect
A point where neither curve is defined
A point located far outside both graphed curves

quiz.q: Why might solving a system of nonlinear equations produce more solutions than a similar linear system?
options: Every nonlinear system always has exactly zero solutions
Nonlinear equations can never intersect with any other equation
Curved graphs such as parabolas and circles can intersect a line at more than one point
Curves are not allowed to intersect straight lines under any circumstance

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Variable Mass Systems and the Rocket Equation
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: a variable mass system, such as a rocket expelling burned fuel, requires an extended form of Newtons second law that accounts for mass leaving or joining the system, leading to the rocket equation, which relates a rockets change in velocity to the exhaust speed and the ratio of its initial to final mass.

quiz.q: What kind of physical system does the rocket equation describe?
options: A variable mass system, such as a rocket expelling burned fuel
A system consisting of a single point mass with no fuel or propulsion
A system with no motion of any kind
A system with a perfectly constant, unchanging total mass

quiz.q: Why is an extended form of Newtons second law needed for a system like a rocket?
options: Because it accounts for mass leaving or joining the system over time
Because rockets experience no external or internal forces at all
Because the systems total mass never changes in any rocket problem
Because Newtons second law cannot be applied to any physical system involving motion

quiz.q: What two quantities does the rocket equation relate to a rockets change in velocity?
options: The rockets electric charge and magnetic field strength
The temperature of the surrounding atmosphere alone
The colour of the rocket and its total surface area
The exhaust speed and the ratio of its initial to final mass

quiz.q: How does the rocket equation relate to the conservation of momentum studied in an earlier batch?
options: The rocket equation has no connection to momentum conservation of any kind
The rocket equation is derived by applying conservation of momentum to the combined system of the rocket and the fuel it expels
Conservation of momentum only applies to systems with constant mass and can never be extended to a rocket
The rocket equation replaces the need for momentum conservation entirely

quiz.q: Why is the rocket equation an important result for space travel and propulsion engineering?
options: It quantifies how much velocity change a rocket can achieve based on its fuel mass ratio and exhaust speed
It has no practical application to designing or analyzing real spacecraft
Exhaust speed has no influence on a rockets achievable change in velocity
The rocket equation applies only to objects that never lose any mass

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: Imagism and the Haiku's Influence on Modern Verse
subjects.summary: Traces the early-20th-century Imagist movement, with its call for precise, unadorned images and its debt to Japanese haiku, and asks students to analyze and write compressed, image-centered poems that avoid abstraction and ornament.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Poetry: Imagism and the Haiku's Influence on Modern Verse

quiz.q: The Imagist movement, associated with poets like Ezra Pound, called for poetry that:
options: used elaborate, ornamental language and long narrative arcs
told a moral fable through extended allegory
presented a precise, concrete image with minimal abstraction or excess wording
rhymed every line according to a strict meter

quiz.q: Imagist poets drew significant inspiration from which non-Western poetic form?
options: Chinese regulated verse exclusively
The Persian ghazal
The Arabic qasida
The Japanese haiku

quiz.q: A traditional haiku's structure is most commonly described as:
options: a single long line built on internal rhyme
fourteen lines ending in a rhymed couplet
four stanzas of equal length joined by a refrain
three unrhymed lines, often patterned 5-7-5 syllables, capturing a single moment

quiz.q: Which line best exemplifies an Imagist aesthetic?
options: 'The theme of this poem is loneliness and regret, as I will now explain'
'Petals on a wet, black bough'
'Oh, how my heart doth ache with sorrows deep and vast tonight'
'Once upon a time, in a kingdom far away, there lived a poet'

quiz.q: What is a central difference between Imagism and the confessional poetry studied earlier in this course?
options: Imagism requires strict rhyme, while confessional poetry never rhymes
Imagism favors compressed, external imagery over sustained autobiographical disclosure
There is no meaningful difference between the two movements
Confessional poetry never uses imagery of any kind

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Trigonometric Identities: Pythagorean Identities
subjects.summary: Students prove and apply the Pythagorean trigonometric identities, including sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and its derived forms, to simplify expressions and verify other trigonometric identities.

quiz.q: Which identity is a direct consequence of the Pythagorean theorem applied to the unit circle?
options: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
sinθ · cosθ = 1
sinθ + cosθ = 1
sin²θ - cos²θ = 1

quiz.q: Dividing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ produces which identity?
options: tan²θ - 1 = sec²θ
tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ
1 + cot²θ = csc²θ
sin²θ = 1 - tan²θ

quiz.q: Simplify sin²θ / (1 - cos²θ).
options: 2sinθ
cos²θ

quiz.q: If sinθ = 3/5 and θ is in the first quadrant, what is cosθ using the Pythagorean identity?
Which expression is equivalent to 1 + cot²θ?
options: 1 - sin²θ
sec²θ
tan²θ
csc²θ

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Calculus: Curve Sketching Using the First and Second Derivative Tests
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Math strand: curve sketching uses the first derivative to locate increasing and decreasing intervals and turning points, and the second derivative to determine concavity and inflection points, combining both tests to produce an accurate graph of a function without plotting every point.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Calculus: Curve Sketching Using the First and Second Derivative Tests

quiz.q: What does the first derivative test help locate on a graph?
options: Increasing and decreasing intervals and turning points
The total number of variables in the function
The name of the mathematician who defined the function
The exact colour used to draw the graph

quiz.q: What does the second derivative test help determine?
options: Concavity and inflection points
The domain of a completely unrelated function
The exact y-intercept only
The number of times a graph must be redrawn

quiz.q: Why might a mathematician sketch a curve using derivative tests rather than plotting many points?
options: It guarantees the graph will contain no curves of any kind
Derivative tests remove the need for a graph to have any shape
It produces an accurate graph efficiently by identifying key features directly
Plotting points is always mathematically impossible

quiz.q: What indicates a local maximum when using the first derivative test?
options: The derivative changes from positive to negative at that point
The function is undefined at every point nearby
The derivative changes from negative to more negative
The derivative remains zero across the entire domain

quiz.q: What combined information do the first and second derivative tests provide together?
options: The colour scheme used in a textbook diagram
A complete picture of a functions shape, including turning points and concavity
A list of unrelated historical dates
The exact numeric value of every point on the graph

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: RLC Circuits and the Physics of Damped Oscillation
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: an RLC circuit combines a resistor, inductor, and capacitor, so that the natural oscillation of energy between the inductors magnetic field and the capacitors electric field is gradually damped by resistive energy loss, producing behaviour that ranges from underdamped ringing to overdamped decay depending on the component values.

quiz.q: What three components make up an RLC circuit?
options: Two capacitors and a single wire with no resistor or inductor
A resistor, an inductor, and a capacitor
Only two resistors and no other component
A battery and a light bulb with no resistor, inductor, or capacitor

quiz.q: What effect does the resistor have on the natural oscillation of an RLC circuit compared to a pure LC circuit?
options: It causes the oscillation to grow without bound over time
It instantly stops all current flow in the circuit
It has no effect whatsoever on the oscillation
It gradually damps the oscillation through resistive energy loss

quiz.q: What range of behaviour can an RLC circuit exhibit depending on its component values?
options: Behaviour with no dependence on the circuits component values at all
A behaviour in which current always increases without any limit
Behaviour ranging from underdamped ringing to overdamped decay
Only a single fixed behaviour regardless of component values

quiz.q: How does the RLC circuit relate to the LC circuit studied in an earlier batch?
options: Adding a resistor to an LC circuit has no effect on its oscillatory behaviour
The RLC circuit and the LC circuit are identical, with no distinguishing components
The RLC circuit builds on the LC circuits energy-exchanging oscillation by adding a resistor, which introduces damping that a pure LC circuit does not have
The LC circuit always includes more damping than the RLC circuit

quiz.q: Why is understanding damping in an RLC circuit important for designing practical electronic devices?
options: Damping has no relevance to the design of any practical electronic device
RLC circuits are never used in any real electronic application
The degree of damping cannot be influenced by any of the circuits component values
Controlling the degree of damping allows engineers to shape how a circuit responds over time, which matters for applications such as filters

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Georgic and the Poetry of Agricultural Labour
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: the georgic is a classical poetic form, exemplified by Virgils Georgics, that treats the practical labour of farming, land, and rural life with dignity and technical detail, offering a companion and counterpoint to the pastorals idealized vision of leisurely rural ease.

quiz.q: What subject matter does a georgic poem typically treat?
options: Warfare and heroic combat exclusively
Purely urban settings with no connection to land or agriculture
Abstract philosophical argument with no reference to physical labour
The practical labour of farming, land, and rural life

quiz.q: With which classical poet is the georgic form especially associated?
options: Virgil
A purely modern poet writing after the twentieth century
A poet with no connection to classical Rome
A dramatist rather than a poet of rural life

quiz.q: What quality does georgic poetry typically bring to its depiction of agricultural work?
options: An exclusive focus on urban industry rather than land
Dignity and technical detail
A total absence of any practical detail about farming
Complete disdain and mockery of any rural labour

quiz.q: How does the georgic compare to the pastoral tradition studied in an earlier batch?
options: Both concern rural life, but the pastoral idealizes leisurely ease while the georgic focuses on the dignity and practical detail of agricultural labour
The georgic and the pastoral have no thematic relationship to rural life at all
The two traditions describe exactly the same idealized, leisurely vision of rural life
The pastoral tradition focuses on technical farming labour rather than ease

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose the georgic mode to depict labour rather than the idealized ease of the pastoral?
options: Georgic poetry is incapable of conveying any meaningful relationship to land
The georgic mode always avoids any depiction of the natural world
Focusing on the dignity and detail of real agricultural work can convey a more grounded relationship between people and the land
Choosing the georgic mode removes any possibility of poetic craft

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Compound Angle Formulas
subjects.summary: Students derive and apply the compound (sum and difference) angle formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent to evaluate exact trigonometric values for non-special angles and to simplify expressions.

quiz.q: Which is the correct compound angle formula for sin(A+B)?
options: sinA cosB - cosA sinB
cosA cosB - sinA sinB
cosA cosB + sinA sinB
sinA cosB + cosA sinB

quiz.q: Use the compound angle formula to find the exact value of cos(75°) using cos(45°+30°).
Which identity correctly expresses tan(A-B)?
options: (tanA - tanB)/(1 + tanA tanB)
(tanA + tanB)/(1 - tanA tanB)
(tanA - tanB)/(1 - tanA tanB)
tanA - tanB

quiz.q: Evaluate sin(15°) exactly using sin(45°-30°).
Simplify cos(x)cos(y) - sin(x)sin(y) using a compound angle formula.
options: cos(x+y)
sin(x-y)
cos(x-y)
sin(x+y)

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Vectors: The Scalar Triple Product and Volume
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Math strand: the scalar triple product combines the dot product and cross product of three vectors to produce a single number equal to the volume of the parallelepiped formed by those vectors, providing a way to test whether three vectors lie in the same plane.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Vectors: The Scalar Triple Product and Volume

quiz.q: What does the scalar triple product of three vectors produce?
options: A matrix with no numerical value
A new vector perpendicular to all three original vectors
A single point with no coordinates
A single number equal to the volume of the parallelepiped formed by the vectors

quiz.q: Which two vector operations are combined to compute the scalar triple product?
options: The dot product and the cross product
Multiplication by a scalar only
Addition and subtraction only
Division of two vectors

quiz.q: What does a scalar triple product equal to zero indicate about three vectors?
options: The vectors cannot be graphed in three dimensions
The vectors are coplanar, lying in the same plane
The vectors form a perfect cube with maximum volume
The vectors are always perpendicular to one another

quiz.q: What geometric shape is associated with the scalar triple product?
options: A parallelepiped
A regular pentagon
A perfect sphere
A single straight line

quiz.q: Why is the scalar triple product useful in three-dimensional geometry?
options: It eliminates the need to ever use a cross product
It provides a way to calculate volume and test whether vectors are coplanar
It can only be used to measure angles in two dimensions
It has no connection to volume or coplanarity of any kind

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Science: Epidemiology and Disease Modelling
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand: epidemiology studies how diseases spread through populations, using mathematical models to predict outbreaks and help guide effective public health responses.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Science: Epidemiology and Disease Modelling

quiz.q: What does epidemiology study?
options: How diseases spread through populations
How plants convert sunlight into food
How rocks form over millions of years
A concept unrelated to science

quiz.q: Do epidemiologists use mathematical models to predict outbreaks?
options: Yes
No, epidemiology never uses any mathematical models
A concept unrelated to epidemiology
Disease outbreaks can never be predicted in any way

quiz.q: Can disease modelling help guide effective public health responses?
options: Yes
A concept unrelated to epidemiology
Public health responses never rely on any scientific modelling
No, disease modelling has no connection to public health decisions

quiz.q: Why might epidemiologists track how quickly a disease spreads from person to person?
options: This concept has no connection to epidemiology
Diseases always spread at the exact same rate in every situation
Tracking disease spread never provides any useful information
This information helps predict future spread and guide public health responses

quiz.q: Why is epidemiology considered an important field during a public health emergency?
options: This concept has no relevance to science
Public health emergencies never require any scientific data
It provides critical data to help guide decisions that protect public health
Epidemiology has no relevance during a public health emergency

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Manifesto and the Rhetoric of Collective Declaration
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: a manifesto is a public declaration that boldly asserts a groups beliefs, grievances, and intentions, using confident, often urgent rhetoric and a clear enumerated structure to rally support and announce a program for change.

quiz.q: What is the basic purpose of a manifesto?
options: To present a neutral, uncommitted summary with no clear position
To privately record a single individuals unpublished thoughts
To publicly declare a groups beliefs, grievances, and intentions
To document historical events with no persuasive or declarative purpose

quiz.q: What tone does manifesto rhetoric typically adopt?
options: Confident, often urgent rhetoric
A hesitant, apologetic tone throughout
A tone of complete indifference to its subject
A purely comic, non-serious tone

quiz.q: What structural feature often helps a manifesto organize its claims?
options: A structure identical to a private diary entry
A structure that must always take the form of a single unbroken sentence
A clear enumerated structure
A structure that forbids any organization or listing of ideas

quiz.q: How does the manifesto compare to the jeremiad studied in an earlier batch?
options: The jeremiad always presents a numbered list of demands
Both use forceful public rhetoric to call for change, but the manifesto asserts a forward-looking program while the jeremiad laments a decline from past values
The two forms are identical in structure, tone, and historical origin
A manifesto only ever laments the past with no forward-looking program

quiz.q: Why might a group choose the manifesto form to announce a new movement or cause?
options: Its bold, declarative rhetoric can rally support and clearly define a shared identity and program for an audience
A manifesto is incapable of rallying any audience support
The manifesto form always weakens a groups stated cause
Declarative public rhetoric has no role in announcing a new movement

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Functions: The Error Function and Its Link to the Normal Distribution
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: the error function is a special function defined by an integral that has no elementary closed form, used to express the cumulative probability of the normal distribution and to describe diffusion and heat-conduction processes that follow a similar bell-shaped pattern.

quiz.q: How is the error function defined?
options: By a purely geometric construction with no reference to integration
By an integral that has no elementary closed form
By a ratio of two integers with no integral involved
By a simple polynomial expression with a finite number of terms

quiz.q: What probability concept is the error function closely used to express?
options: The cumulative probability of the normal distribution
The exact value of a discrete binomial probability
The probability of a single coin flip landing heads
A probability that is always exactly equal to one

quiz.q: Besides probability, what kind of physical process can the error function help describe?
options: Diffusion and heat-conduction processes
The vibration of a plucked string
The orbital motion of planets around a star
The refraction of light through a lens

quiz.q: How does the error function relate to the normal distribution studied in an earlier batch?
options: The error function replaces the need for the normal distribution entirely
The two concepts have no mathematical relationship whatsoever
The error function provides the mathematical tool used to compute cumulative probabilities under the normal distributions bell-shaped curve
The normal distribution is defined without any reference to integration of any kind

quiz.q: Why is it useful to have a named special function like the error function, even though it lacks an elementary closed form?
options: Naming a function with no elementary closed form provides no practical benefit
It provides a standard, well-studied way to work with and compute an integral that otherwise cannot be expressed using elementary functions
The error function is identical to an elementary polynomial function
Special functions without elementary closed forms can never be computed or tabulated

subjects.subject: Calculus
subjects.title: Data Management: The Birthday Problem and Probability
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: the birthday problem is a classic probability puzzle that calculates the surprisingly high likelihood that at least two people in a moderately sized group share the same birthday, illustrating how quickly probabilities can grow as the number of possible pairs in a group increases.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Data Management: The Birthday Problem and Probability

quiz.q: What does the birthday problem calculate?
options: The probability that at least two people in a group share the same birthday
The probability that no person in the world has ever shared a birthday
The exact date on which the most people in the world were born
The average number of days between two peoples birthdays

quiz.q: Why is the result of the birthday problem often described as surprising?
options: The birthday problem always produces a probability of exactly 100 percent
The probability of a shared birthday is always exactly zero in any group
A shared birthday is impossible unless a group contains at least 365 people
The probability of a shared birthday becomes quite high with a relatively small group, far fewer than 365 people

quiz.q: With approximately 23 people in a room, what is roughly true about the probability that at least two share a birthday?
options: The probability is less than 1 percent
The probability is just over 50 percent
The probability is exactly 0 percent
The probability is always exactly 23 percent

quiz.q: Why does the number of possible pairs in a group grow quickly as more people are added?
options: Adding more people to a group never changes the number of possible pairs
Pairs can only be formed between exactly two people in the entire group
The number of pairs in a group always increases at exactly the same rate as the number of people
Each new person can be paired with every other person already in the group, so the number of pairs increases much faster than the number of people

quiz.q: How is the probability that at least two people share a birthday typically calculated?
options: By first finding the probability that no two people share a birthday, then subtracting that value from one
By assuming every person in the group was born on the exact same day
The probability of a shared birthday cannot be calculated using any mathematical method
By directly counting every possible birthday combination for every person on Earth

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.title: Lens Aberrations: Chromatic and Spherical Distortion
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Physics strand: a lens aberration is a deviation from perfect image formation, with chromatic aberration arising because a lens refracts different wavelengths of light by different amounts, and spherical aberration arising because rays passing through the edges of a spherically shaped lens focus at a different point than rays near its centre.

quiz.q: What is a lens aberration, in general terms?
options: A deviation that only affects the colour of the lens itself, with no effect on any image
A deviation from perfect image formation by a lens
A property that only appears in lenses with no curvature whatsoever
A term describing a lens that has no optical properties at all

quiz.q: What causes chromatic aberration in a lens?
options: The lens refracts different wavelengths of light by different amounts
The lens absorbs all wavelengths of light equally, producing no image
The lens has no interaction with light of any wavelength
Chromatic aberration is caused entirely by the lenses temperature

quiz.q: What causes spherical aberration in a lens?
options: Spherical aberration is caused by a lens absorbing all incoming light
Rays passing through the edges of a spherically shaped lens focus at a different point than rays near its centre
Spherical aberration only occurs in lenses with no curvature
All rays passing through a spherical lens always focus at exactly the same point with no exception

quiz.q: How does chromatic aberration relate to the refraction studied earlier in this course?
options: Chromatic aberration only occurs in the complete absence of any refraction
Chromatic aberration arises directly from the wavelength-dependent refraction, or dispersion, of light as it passes through a lens
Chromatic aberration has no connection to the refraction of light at all
Refraction affects every wavelength of light in exactly the same way, with no dependence on colour

quiz.q: Why is understanding lens aberrations important for designing optical instruments, such as telescopes and microscopes studied in an earlier batch?
options: Aberrations have no impact on the image quality produced by an optical instrument
Lens aberrations can only occur in instruments with no lenses at all
Correcting for aberrations, often using combinations of different lens shapes and materials, is necessary to produce sharp images in precision instruments
High-quality optical instruments never need to account for any lens aberration

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Analysis: Meme Culture and Compressed Visual Rhetoric
subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: an internet meme compresses a cultural reference, image, and short text into a highly shareable, rapidly mutating unit of communication, relying on shared context and irony to convey meaning far beyond what its brief surface content states directly.

quiz.q: What elements does an internet meme typically compress into a single unit?
options: A lengthy, uncompressed academic essay
A cultural reference, image, and short text
A single word with no image or reference
An entire feature-length film with no compression at all

quiz.q: What quality allows memes to spread and change rapidly across audiences?
options: Their requirement of lengthy, formal publication before sharing
Their total lack of any visual or textual content
Their complete resistance to being copied or altered
Their highly shareable, rapidly mutating format

quiz.q: What do memes often rely on to convey meaning beyond their literal surface content?
options: Shared context and irony
A complete absence of any shared cultural reference
Strictly literal, unambiguous statements with no irony
Formal academic citation of sources

quiz.q: How does meme culture compare to the political speechwriting studied in an earlier batch?
options: Political speechwriting relies entirely on irony and rapid mutation
Memes are always formally delivered as spoken addresses
The two forms are identical in structure, length, and delivery
Both use deliberately chosen language and imagery to persuade, though memes rely on rapid visual-textual compression and irony rather than sustained oratory

quiz.q: Why might understanding meme rhetoric be considered a relevant media literacy skill?
options: Media literacy has no connection to visual or internet culture
Memes always convey their full meaning literally with no need for interpretation
Memes can shape public opinion and cultural conversation rapidly, so recognizing how they compress and mutate meaning helps a reader interpret them critically
Memes have no influence on public opinion or cultural conversation

subjects.subject: AdvancedFunctions
subjects.title: Statistics: The Monty Hall Problem and Conditional Probability Revisited
subjects.summary: Grade 12 Advanced Functions strand: the Monty Hall problem is a classic probability puzzle in which a contestant chooses one of three doors, one door is revealed to be empty, and switching to the remaining unopened door counterintuitively doubles the contestants probability of winning, illustrating how new information changes conditional probability.

quiz.q: In the classic setup of the Monty Hall problem, how many doors does a contestant initially choose from?
options: Two doors
Three doors
Five doors
A number of doors that changes randomly each round

quiz.q: What counterintuitive result does the Monty Hall problem demonstrate about switching doors after one is revealed to be empty?
options: Switching has no effect at all on the contestants probability of winning
Switching doubles the contestants probability of winning compared to staying with the original choice
Staying with the original door always doubles the winning probability instead
Switching always guarantees a loss for the contestant

quiz.q: What general probability concept does the Monty Hall problem illustrate?
options: That all doors always retain exactly equal probability regardless of new information
That conditional probability never changes once an initial choice is made
How new information changes conditional probability
That probability calculations are impossible once any information is revealed

quiz.q: How does the Monty Hall problem relate to conditional probability and independence, studied in an earlier batch?
options: It provides a concrete, famous example of how revealing new information changes a conditional probability

subjects.subject: Physics

A planet sweeps out a constantly increasing area regardless of time elapsed
A planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times
The area swept out depends only on the planets colour

quiz.q: What relationship does Keplers third law establish?

The square of a planets orbital period is proportional to the cube of its average orbital distance
The cube of the orbital period equals the square of the planets mass

quiz.q: How do Keplers laws relate to the general treatment of orbital mechanics studied in an earlier batch?

subjects.subject: English

subjects.summary: Grade 12 English strand: Horatian satire uses a light, witty, good-humoured tone to gently mock human folly, while Juvenalian satire uses a harsh, indignant, and often bitter tone to attack vice and corruption, giving satirists two distinct rhetorical registers for the same critical purpose.

quiz.q: What tone characterizes Horatian satire?
options: A light, witty, good-humoured tone that gently mocks human folly
A tone entirely devoid of any humour or wit
A harsh, bitter tone aimed at severe moral condemnation
A tone that avoids commenting on human behaviour altogether

quiz.q: What tone characterizes Juvenalian satire?
options: A tone that never addresses any moral or social failing
A gentle, affectionate tone with no critical edge
A harsh, indignant, and often bitter tone that attacks vice and corruption
A tone limited strictly to praise with no criticism at all

quiz.q: What do Horatian and Juvenalian satire share despite their different tones?
options: Both avoid any critical or corrective purpose whatsoever
Both use satire for the same broad critical purpose of exposing human folly or vice

Both are written exclusively in formal academic prose with no wit

quiz.q: How does the Horatian and Juvenalian distinction compare to Menippean satire studied in an earlier batch?
options: Juvenalian satire and Menippean satire share an identical tone in every case

Menippean satire is simply another name for the Horatian mode
The three modes describe the exact same satiric technique with no distinction

quiz.q: Why is it useful for a writer or reader to distinguish between Horatian and Juvenalian satiric tone?
options: Recognizing the intended tone shapes how sharply a satire is meant to sting and how an audience is meant to respond to its criticism
Tone is irrelevant to the effectiveness of satire as a literary mode
Every satirical work uses exactly the same tone regardless of its author or purpose
The distinction has no bearing on how a satirical text should be read or written
